title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for Yoga and Pilates
audience: Yoga and Pilates teachers who need a base hourly rate, a class or course rate and a minimum charge before they quote
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, and calculate the time available to bill.
Calculate a base hourly rate from the teacher's own costs and income target, then compare it with public local evidence.
Set a minimum charge for short bookings and explain it to a client before the class.

instruction.heading: Factors that move the rate
instruction.body: A teacher's rate depends on training and registration, the style and level taught, class size, the room available and the local price range. AUSactive's yoga registration asks for a certificate from a recognised yoga education provider and current CPR and first aid. A provisional 200-hour entry also needs at least 10 hours of supervised practicum and an endorsement letter (AUSactive, modified 1 May 2026). Yoga Australia and Yoga Alliance certificates are accepted. For Pilates, the Pilates Association of Australia says a Certificate III or IV in Fitness does not cover teaching Pilates, and that group mat or reformer classes need a Pilates-specific certificate (PAA, 1 August 2023). Those qualifications affect what you can teach and what an insurer will cover, so the training you hold shapes the rate you can defend. Local price evidence comes from public studio lists. Central Yoga's fortnightly memberships run from $40 for one class a week to $112 for unlimited classes, and its single in-person class is $28 (Central Yoga, undated). Compare only with trained, insured teachers.

instruction.heading: Counting the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Teachers often price as though every hour can be taught and paid for. Set-up, pack-down, travel between halls, marketing, admin, cleaning mats and props, insurance paperwork and continuing professional development are not billable. AUSactive's yoga registration asks for 10 CPD for a 12-month registration, or 20 CPD for a 24-month registration, plus CPR every year and first aid every three years (AUSactive, modified 1 May 2026). That time is non-billable and must be counted. Jobber says billable time typically makes up 60 to 80 per cent of working hours (Jobber, published 5 November 2024, modified 20 July 2026). That is a general range, not a yoga figure, so check it against your own log. For example, if 6 of every 9 paid hours are teaching, the costs of all 9 hours must come out of 6 billable hours, so the rate is 1.5 times the rate for a fully billable week.

instruction.heading: Building the rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add the annual costs of running the teaching business, such as insurance, registration, CPR and first aid training, props, booking software, marketing and accounting, to the income you need. Divide the total by billable hours to reach the base rate. Xero's method starts from the take-home pay you want, adds business costs and super, then divides by billable hours (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Hall hire is an hourly cost set by the venue. Mornington Peninsula Shire's 2026/27 community hall rate is $16 an hour, and its commercial hall rates are listed at $38, $32, $84 and $73 an hour, with garbled labels (Mornington Peninsula Shire, 2026/27). Confirm the rate that applies to you before you add it to the price. Review the base rate each quarter.

instruction.heading: Setting a minimum charge for short bookings
instruction.body: A short workshop, a small class or a private session still needs set-up, travel and admin. Hall hire can also carry set-up and cleaning charges. The same council schedule lists set-up per booking at $250 to $755 depending on size, a bond from $250 to $1,000, and a minimum cleaning charge of $500 (Mornington Peninsula Shire, 2026/27). Charges like these mean a short booking costs far more per hour than a long one, so check the hire terms before you publish a minimum. A contractor pricing guide suggests setting the minimum from the full cost of the visit, dividing that cost by one minus the target margin, with the minimum covering travel, set-up and clean-up (Contractor+, 23 September 2026). That guide labels its figures illustrative, so this lesson uses the method only. State the minimum before the booking, in writing, and explain what it covers.

instruction.heading: Reviewing the rate and comparing with others
instruction.body: Business Victoria recommends reviewing prices about every three months, to check that they still suit the business and its customers, and it warns against assuming that a rival's prices are right (Business Victoria, no date shown). Xero recommends reviewing prices at least once a year (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). Compare your rate only with trained, insured teachers, because credentials, students and costs differ. Honour packages and memberships already sold at the old rate.

procedure: Log teaching and non-teaching hours for one month, then estimate the year's billable hours.
List the annual running costs, including insurance, registration, CPR and first aid, CPD, props, booking software, marketing, accounting and hall hire.
Add the income needed, including leave and tax allowances confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by billable hours to find the base rate.
Set a minimum charge that covers travel, set-up and admin for a short booking, and state it in writing.
Review the rate each quarter, and record any change and the reason for it.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A teacher's diary shows six teaching hours a week. She also spends about three hours a week on admin, marketing, CPD and travel (illustrative). She plans to price as though all nine hours could be billed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the assumption do to the rate, and what should she do instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: The costs of nine hours of work must come out of six billable hours. A rate built on nine hours would be two-thirds of the rate built on six hours, so it understates the rate by about a third. She should build the rate from her six billable hours, add her registration, CPR and first aid, CPD, insurance and hall costs, then check the result against public studio prices from trained, insured teachers and against her minimum charge before she publishes it.

equipmentAndPpe: Log of teaching and non-teaching hours for one month
Price sheet with the base rate, the class or course rate and the minimum charge

commonErrors.error: Setting a rate from a published average or a competitor's figure without checking the costs.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the base rate from the teacher's own costs and billable hours, then compare it with public local evidence.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract the non-billable time before dividing.

commonErrors.error: Taking short bookings at the same rate, without covering travel, set-up and hall charges.
commonErrors.prevention: Set and state a minimum charge that covers travel, set-up, admin and any hall set-up or cleaning charge.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Price display rules come from the Australian Consumer Law, as summarised in the ACCC's guidance on setting prices. That guidance does not cover minimum or call-out charges, or what counts as a fair term. Check those points against current ACCC guidance or a legal adviser before publishing a price sheet.
Hall hire and bond terms vary by council and venue. The council schedule used here has garbled commercial labels, so confirm each rate before you rely on it.

Health screening: the Pilates Association of Australia says Pilates sessions should begin with a health screening. This is association guidance, not a verified legal standard. No yoga screening standard was verified.
Tax and superannuation for employed teachers and for the owner: confirm with a registered tax agent. This lesson does not state tax treatment.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged or estimated month, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the teacher's costs and income target, and is compared with public local evidence.
A minimum charge is set and stated before any short booking.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the class or course rate, the minimum charge and the review date
summary: Price from billable hours, not from paid hours.
Build the rate from costs and a stated income target, then check it against public local evidence.
Set and state a minimum charge for short bookings.

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner can bill only some of the paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower and so the client pays less per job
From billable hours, so the costs and income are covered by the work that can be billed
From the average published on a website and from the rate listed by the nearest competitor
From the rate the owner wishes the market would pay and the owner's own mood on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Why set a minimum charge for short jobs?
options: Because short jobs need travel but no setup time at all and the admin takes no time
Because travel, setup and admin time does not shrink with the size of the job
Because clients expect every job to cost the same amount, whatever its size
Because a minimum charge replaces a written quote for every job the owner takes

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best source for checking a base hourly rate?
options: A single published national average from the largest trade body
The owner's own costs and billable hours, compared with local evidence
A friend's rate, without checking the costs or the local market
The rate shown on the first page of a bidding site this week

sourceReferences: AUSactive, 'Yoga professional', https://ausactive.org.au/membership/yoga-professional/, modified 1 May 2026. Supports: registration requirements; CPD of 10 for 12 months or 20 for 24 months; CPR yearly and first aid every three years.

Pilates Association of Australia, 'Frequently asked questions', https://pilates.org.au/?p=16699, 1 August 2023. Supports: Certificate III or IV in Fitness does not cover teaching Pilates; Pilates-specific training needed for group mat or reformer classes.
Central Yoga, 'Prices', https://centralyoga.com.au/prices, undated. Vendor price list as shown at fetch; not a market rate.

Jobber, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Supports: billable time at about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; general range.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: starting from take-home pay plus costs and super; dividing by billable hours; review at least yearly.
business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs in the hourly figure.

Mornington Peninsula Shire, 'Venue hire fees and charges 2026-27', https://www.mornpen.vic.gov.au/files/assets/public2/v/6/community-services/halls-for-hire/docs/venue-hire-fees-and-charges-2026-27.pdf, no publication date shown; 2026/27 schedule, GST inclusive. Commercial labels garbled; confirm with the council.

Contractor+, 'Minimum Service Call Charge: A Contractor's Pricing Guide', https://contractorplus.app/blog/minimum-service-call-charge, 23 September 2026. Supports the method only; figures labelled illustrative and not used.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Supports: review about every three months; do not assume rivals' prices are right.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Not verified: insurance premiums; the Pilates Association's screening and cover statements; tax treatment of leave and superannuation; Fitness Australia rules; the NSW and Victorian rules where they apply.
